traits.note: Sargent (1922, Acoelorraphe, p. 105): trees with tall, slender, often clustered stems clothed for years in the sheathing bases of fallen leaves, the leaves nearly round and fan-cut; A. wrightii a tree of numerous stems forming great thickets. Mabberley (2017) places it in subfamily III, tribe Trachycarpeae.

traits.leaf_division.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.
